claims.finding: LB and TDB0 define an affine TCB-to-TDB map; at the 1977 geocentric origin TDB differs from TT by TDB0.
claims.reason: An exact coordinate definition supplies no measured ephemeris uncertainty.

claims.finding: LG is a fixed defining rate constant for TT relative to TCG.
claims.reason: Defining LG does not certify the physical realization TT(TAI) or a station clock.

claims.finding: Other ephemerides can imply residual geocentric TDB-TT drift; the stated expectation is 1 ns per year.
claims.reason: An expectation about rate is not a DE440t absolute-error bound or an independently measured drift.

claims.finding: The library documentation instead gives 1 ns per century for possible drift with future ephemerides.
claims.reason: The rate statement differs from IAU 2006 note 2; do not silently substitute either as a hard bound.

claims.finding: The documented 3 ns comparison applies over 1950-2050 against DE405-based integrated time ephemerides.
claims.reason: DE405-relative model accuracy is not a physical DE440t, site-clock or arrival error certificate.

claims.finding: The stated 0.2 ps quasi-periodic phase accuracy has spatial and formulation conditions; astronomical input errors can be larger.
claims.reason: The truncated ten-body site model and its uncertain inputs have not been shown to satisfy that complete formulation.

claims.finding: The integrated time transformation uses explicit normalization, external potentials and relativistic terms.
claims.reason: These equations do not themselves provide a complete numerical uncertainty bound for our archived DE440t geocentric values.

claims.finding: CSPICE and jplephem agree on archived DE440t evaluations while sharing the same physical model and coefficients.
claims.reason: Implementation agreement is not independent evidence of physical error.
